home.statement: I build small, focused apps and games for Android — the kind that do one thing properly and stay out of your way. Everything here is designed, written and shipped solo.
home.supportDesc: Every app here is built solo. A coffee keeps the next one coming.

project.joinClosedTesting: Not public yet — tap to join closed testing on Google Play

listkeeper.description: Most list apps grow until they need a tutorial. ListKeeper goes the other way: a fast, clean place to keep your lists, with nothing bolted on that you'll never open. Make a list, check things off, get on with your day.
features: Clean, uncluttered interface
Fast and lightweight
Works entirely offline
Optional Premium upgrade

whataretheodds.tagline: Beat the odds. Climb the ladder.
whataretheodds.description: Start at 1 in 10. Guess the number and 1 in 20 unlocks. Keep going and the ladder runs all the way to 1 in 10,000 — then to Custom odds, where you pick your own impossible number. Most attempts fail. That's the game.
features: Eleven tiers from 1 in 10 to Custom odds
Global leaderboards via Play Games
Attempts refill over time, even while closed
Achievements and friend comparisons

pixelwrangler.tagline: Tap fast. Draft a build. Climb the storm.
pixelwrangler.description: The feed is broken and wild pixels are pouring out of the glitch. Tap them out of the air before they escape, dodge what's hiding in the storm, and climb one 50-wave mountain past ten bosses. After every wave you draft one of three cards — stack three of a signal and a Resonance changes the rules rather than the numbers. Take the corrupted card for more power and a permanent fault, or play it clean. A run that ends badly still pays out.
features: A 50-wave climb with a checkpoint every ten
One of three upgrade cards drafted after every wave
Ten bosses, each with a single opening to find
Corrupted cards: more power, a permanent cost
Shards from every run, spent on a perk tree
Plays offline — no account, no timers

oretoorbit.tagline: Mine a flat world. Build a rocket out of shapes. Leave.
oretoorbit.description: You're stuck in a flat, two-dimensional world, and the way out is a craft you fabricate from raw geometry. Mine the ground for dots, spend them at the bench — a square is hull, a triangle is a nozzle, a line is plumbing — then fly the thing you built out of the atmosphere. Nothing in it is a sprite: every object is a primitive, and the sky, the light and the glow on all of them come from one number, how much air is left above you.
features: A Box2D physics sandbox, from the first dig to the burn
Assemble a craft cell by cell, then find out what you got wrong
Round worlds — walk far enough and you come back to your own shaft
One continuous ascent: bright day at the surface, glowing lines in the void

teaser.rule: Shape is form. Colour is function.
teaser.note: The whole game is four objects — point, line, triangle, square — and what a part does comes from what it is made of, so a red triangle is a nozzle and a blue square is a battery. New mechanics arrive as new materials rather than as new art. In development; no release date yet.
teaser.alt: A stick figure on a curving horizon, ore glowing under the ground, and a rocket built from squares and triangles climbing into a starfield.

homepool.tagline: Track your pool. Never guess when it's due.
homepool.description: homepool is a self-hosted pool and spa maintenance tracker: log water measurements and treatments, get sanitizer-aware target ranges and dosing advice, and see it all from a clean dashboard — your data never leaves your own server. A first-class Home Assistant integration brings your readings and maintenance schedule into your existing smart home, with actionable push notifications when something's due.
features: Water status board with ideal ranges and dosing advice per parameter
Configurable maintenance schedule — backwash, filter checks, and anything else you track
Home Assistant integration with a purpose-built Lovelace card
Actionable push notifications that mark a task done right from the alert
Self-hosted with one Docker command — your data stays on your own server
